description: Na₅Fe₂P₂(CO₇)₂ crystallizes in the triclinic P̅1 space group. There are five inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.32-2.74 Å. In the second Na site, Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.41-2.93 Å. In the third Na site, Na is bonded to seven O atoms to form distorted NaO₇ pentagonal bipyramids that share  a cornercorner with one FeO₆ octahedra, corners with two equivalent PO₄ tetrahedra,  an edgeedge with one FeO₆ octahedra,  an edgeedge with one PO₄ tetrahedra, and  a faceface with one FeO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 67°. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.33-2.80 Å. In the fourth Na site, Na is bonded in a 7-coordinate geometry to seven O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.36-2.84 Å. In the fifth Na site, Na is bonded in a 7-coordinate geometry to seven O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.23-2.83 Å. There are two inequivalent Fe sites. In the first Fe site, Fe is bonded to six O atoms to form distorted FeO₆ octahedra that share  a cornercorner with one NaO₇ pentagonal bipyramid, corners with four PO₄ tetrahedra, and  a faceface with one NaO₇ pentagonal bipyramid. There are a spread of Fe-O bond distances ranging from 2.07-2.24 Å. In the second Fe site, Fe is bonded to six O atoms to form distorted FeO₆ octahedra that share corners with four PO₄ tetrahedra and  an edgeedge with one NaO₇ pentagonal bipyramid. There are a spread of Fe-O bond distances ranging from 1.97-2.25 Å. There are two inequivalent C sites. In the first C site, C is bonded in a trigonal planar geometry to three O atoms. There are a spread of C-O bond distances ranging from 1.28-1.32 Å. In the second C site, C is bonded in a trigonal planar geometry to three O atoms. There are a spread of C-O bond distances ranging from 1.28-1.31 Å. There are two inequivalent P sites. In the first P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four FeO₆ octahedra and  an edgeedge with one NaO₇ pentagonal bipyramid. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 39-51°. There are a spread of P-O bond distances ranging from 1.55-1.57 Å. In the second P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four FeO₆ octahedra and corners with two equivalent NaO₇ pentagonal bipyramids. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 39-45°. There are two shorter (1.54 Å) and two longer (1.57 Å) P-O bond lengths. There are fourteen inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to four Na and one C atom. In the second O site, O is bonded in a distorted rectangular see-saw-like geometry to three Na and one C atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to three Na, one Fe, and one C atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two Na, one Fe, and one C atom. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a distorted rectangular see-saw-like geometry to two Na, one Fe, and one C atom. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a 1-coordinate geometry to three Na, one Fe, and one C atom. In the seventh O site, O is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to three Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the eighth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the ninth O site, O is bonded in a 1-coordinate geometry to three Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the tenth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the eleventh O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the twelfth O site, O is bonded in a distorted rectangular see-saw-like geometry to two Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the thirteenth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the fourteenth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two Na, one Fe, and one P atom.
